question: What will Japan's national average of influenza cases per sentinel medical institution be for the week ending October 25, 2026?

calls.reasoning: National per-sentinel series this season: wk36 3.29, wk37 5.54, wk38 8.48, wk39 7.17 (Silver Week holiday dip), wk40 11.35, wk41 12.81 (+13%, slowing). Target week ending Oct 25 is two weeks past the last print; Oct 12 Sports Day holiday may depress the intervening week, but the target week is holiday-free. Continued 5-15%/wk growth implies ~14-17; plateau/decline is the main downside, and renewed acceleration in populous Kanto/Hokkaido is the upside. School closures still rising in several prefectures as of Oct 19. Question labels the week as 'week 44', but per the JIHS calendar the week ending Oct 25 is week 43; I forecast the date-defined week and add some upper-tail mass for the mislabel. No human market found on Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi.
calls.dossier:
- JIHS IDWR index (checked 2026-10-20): latest published week is week 41 (Oct 5-11); week 42 (Oct 12-18) expected ~Oct 23; the week ending Oct 25 is JIHS week 43 (question text calls it week 44, but the date and the Oct 30 publication timing match week 43).
- National per-sentinel series 2026-27 (c7service 2026-10-01; resemom/weathernews 2026-10-16): wk36 (Aug31-Sep6) 3.29; wk37 5.54; wk38 8.48; wk39 (Sep21-27, includes Silver Week holidays) 7.17; wk40 11.35; wk41 12.81 (47,746 cases). Week-on-week change: +68%, +53%, -15%, +58%, +13%.
- Prior season comparison: 2025-26 wk38 was 0.80; about 14.9 reached only in the week ending Nov 2, 2025.
- Week 41 prefectures (weathernews 2026-10-16): Okinawa 31.34 (warning), Kanagawa 21.60, Saitama 20.99, Chiba 19.55, Hokkaido 16.21 (+7.00 w/w); Okayama fell to 5.50 (KSB). Over 1,700 schools/childcare facilities had closures.
- Calendar: Monday Oct 12, 2026 is Sports Day (a national holiday) inside week 42, which reduces clinic days; the wk39 holiday week showed a dip. The target week (Oct 19-25) has no holiday.
- 2026-10-19 school closures: Okayama 7 schools newly closed; Toyama cumulative 37 schools; Iwate 15 new facilities in Oct 12-18 (49 for the season vs 6 at this point last year).
- Tokyo IDSC page updated 2026-10-15 through wk41; no numeric week-42 values found.
- Taiwan (UDN 2026-10-20): flu epidemic ongoing there; officials expect it may end by early November (a regional signal only).
- Status quo: continued growth at a slowing rate from 12.81.
- Resolves off the JIHS IDWR national per-sentinel influenza value, first published; not prefecture-level or hospital-based figures.
- Event window: single reading for the week Oct 19-25, 2026; as of Oct 20, day 2 of 7 of that week has elapsed, and two weekly prints (wk42, wk43) are still unpublished.
- Searched, not found: a national week-42 value; a subtype mix breakdown; any prediction market.
calls.reference_class: Two-week-ahead changes in Japan's national flu per-sentinel value during early-season growth phases (e.g., 2023-24 early season, current 2026-27 weeks 36-41)

calls.reasoning: Series 8.48 (wk38), 7.17 (wk39 holiday dip), 11.35 (wk40), 12.81 (wk41, +13%, decelerating). Target is the date-defined week Oct 19-25 (JIHS wk43; question mislabels as 44), holiday-free and two prints ahead. Okinawa past peak and Tokyo long above alert argue for slowing; Kanto/Hokkaido rising and school closures nearly doubling argue for continued growth. Central ~7-10%/wk for two weeks -> ~15. Downside plateau/early peak ~11-12; upside re-acceleration or week-44 interpretation ~20+. No human market found.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the factual series (8.48, 7.17, 11.35, 12.81), that the week ending Oct 25 is JIHS wk43 despite the question's 'week 44' label, that wk42 holds the Sports Day holiday while the target week has none, and that no market exists. Remaining disagreement is a judgment about how fast growth slows (median 15.0-15.8). Run 3's higher centre rests on the school-closures surge and the holiday rebound, both already priced in; Okinawa's decline and the deceleration from +58% to +13% argue against a centre above ~15. I take a median of ~15.1 with a slightly fatter upper tail for the week-label ambiguity (actual wk44 would likely read higher). I keep the runs' ~8-wide dispersion. No web retrieval on this run.
